## Living Workflow Development

> **Last verified:** 2026-08-16 (commit pending — package-specific architecture
> is now co-located with the package and routed to every
> `packages/living-workflow/**` edit). If the generated-skill boundary, state
> root, module ownership, or runtime fanout changes and this fragment is not
> updated in the same commit, stop and fix it.

### Package shape

Living Workflow is a generated content package, not an overlay package:

- `skills/living-workflow/SKILL.md` is the compact router installed into each
  runtime;
- `skills/living-workflow/references/` carries the progressively disclosed
  protocol, schema, changelog, and backlog guide;
- `lib/mkSkill.nix` copies that tree into a derivation and substitutes the
  install-specific `@XDG_STATE_BASE@` token; and
- `modules/homeManager/` and `modules/devenv/` independently contribute the
  generated skill through `lib/ai/mkSkillPackageModule.nix`.

There is deliberately no overlay or static `-content` derivation. The state base
is an evaluation-specific input, so an overlay-time package cannot own the
substitution correctly.

### Generated path contract

`mkSkill.nix` returns the derivation's output path as a string, not the raw
derivation. The shared skill emitters recognize path-like strings and install
the complete directory. Passing the derivation object instead makes those
emitters treat it as text and collapse the tree into one `SKILL.md`.

The builder fingerprints both the skill and reference contents through
`lib/traceSource.nix`; preserve that input. A directory path alone tracks its
listing but can leave a devenv evaluation cache stale after an in-place content
edit.

Home Manager bakes `${config.xdg.stateHome}/living-workflows`. Devenv has no
Home Manager XDG option, so its parity module bakes the shell expression
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/living-workflows`, which resolves when
the skill runs. Ordinary workflows add clone and workflow names below that base.
The framework's own backlog is the documented clone-less first-party exception.

### Program and runtime ownership

`ai.programs.living-workflow.enable = true` is the package gate. It contributes
the skill at `mkDefault` to each supported runtime's
`ai.<runtime>.skills.living-workflow` entry; it never writes the consumer-owned
root `ai.skills` pool. A consumer can replace or null-suppress that entry at one
runtime, or disable the package for that runtime through
`ai.<runtime>.programs.living-workflow.enable = false`.

Home Manager is the primary user-global install path. Devenv is the
project-local parity path. They are separate `evalModules` trees and must each
import the package factory; one backend's contribution is not visible to the
other.

Unlike Stacked Workflows, Living Workflow has no always-loaded routing rule. Its
operations are entered through the installed skill, and the skill description
supplies the selection trigger. Adding a rule merely to duplicate that trigger
would create a second source of truth.
